title: SplitLayout
summary: The standard two-column NavigationSplitView: a list and the detail of the selected item side by side, and one pane at a time on a phone. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For inbox-style screens: browsing a list while reading one item. Drive the detail from the list's selection.
whenNotToUse: For two panes that both stay on screen and are resized by the person use MonarchResizablePanels (see resizable-panels). For a single column of screens use NavigationStack.
api: NavigationSplitView(columnVisibility: Binding<NavigationSplitViewVisibility>, sidebar: () -> Sidebar, detail: () -> Detail)
func navigationSplitViewColumnWidth(min: CGFloat? = nil, ideal: CGFloat, max: CGFloat? = nil) -> some View
func navigationSplitViewStyle(_ style: some NavigationSplitViewStyle) -> some View

states.name: regular width
states.description: Both columns are shown. The selected row has the system's selection background.

states.name: compact width
states.description: One column is shown. Selecting a row pushes the detail, and the system back button returns to the list.

states.name: nothing selected
states.description: The detail column shows the placeholder the app supplies.

appearance: The system draws the columns, the divider between them and the navigation bars. Rows and the detail use Monarch text styles and theme colours; the selection highlight is the system's.
platformNotes: The web SplitLayout takes detailOpen, onBack and backLabel to show one pane below 768 pixels. NavigationSplitView does this itself: at a compact width it becomes a stack, and the back button and its label are the system's. The web's listWidth is navigationSplitViewColumnWidth, which proposes a width; the person cannot drag the column edge on iOS. listLabel and detailLabel are the navigation titles of the columns. Android uses the Material list-detail scaffold.
accessibility: System behaviour: each column is a navigation region with its title as a heading.
System behaviour: at a compact width the back button is named after the list's navigation title.
System behaviour: with a hardware keyboard the arrow keys move the selection in the list.
Give the detail a placeholder text when nothing is selected, so the empty column is not silent.
edgeCases: On a phone in portrait only one column is visible; the selection must be optional so the app can start on the list.
Clearing the selection at a compact width pops back to the list.
A NavigationSplitView inside a NavigationStack shows two navigation bars; make it the root of a scene or a presentation.
